paper_title: Thinking Slow, Fast Scaling Inference Compute with Distilled Reasoners
caption_used: Coverage as a function of the number of completions (k) for Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. All four models exhibit monotonically increasing coverage with additional completions on a logarithmic x-axis from 2^0 to 2^8. The 3B models begin at approximately 0.42 coverage and reach roughly 0.92 at k=256, while the 1B variants start near 0.22 and plateau at approximately 0.72 by k=128 with minimal further gains. Notably, fine-tuning provides a consistent advantage of approximately 5 percentage points for the 1B model throughout the scaling curve, whereas the 3B base and fine-tuned variants remain largely indistinguishable.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the coverage as a function of the number of completions (k) for four different models: Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. The x-axis is labeled "Number of completions (k)" with a logarithmic scale, ranging from 2^0 to 2^8, with tick labels at each power of 2. The y-axis is labeled "Coverage" with a linear scale, ranging from approximately 0.4 to 0.9, with tick labels at intervals of 0.1. The plot includes four lines: Llama-3B (dark blue, solid line), Llama-3B + FT (green triangle markers, solid line), Llama-1B (light blue, solid line), and Llama-1B + FT (green triangle markers, dashed line); Llama-3B starts at around 0.42 coverage at k=1 and reaches approximately 0.92 at k=256, with a steady increase across the x-axis; Llama-3B + FT follows a very similar trend to Llama-3B, also starting at around 0.42 and reaching 0.92 at k=256; Llama-1B begins at approximately 0.22 coverage at k=1 and increases to around 0.67 at k=128, with minimal further gains; Llama-1B + FT starts at around 0.27 and reaches a plateau of approximately 0.72 by k=128.
